angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 507,165 km at 81.32 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.2967 +/- 0.0145 mas (same row, RUWE 1.11): 81.32 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.729 +/- 0.007 solar radii from Eschen et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2345 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2614E/abstract): 507,165 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.727 +/- 0.033 solar masses from Eschen et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2345 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2614E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4687 +/- 60 K from Eschen et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2345 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2614E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Eschen et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2345 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.544.2614E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2345.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.574, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
